title: Five States Account for 86% of Nigeria’s 1,000 Lassa Fever Cases - Brand Icon Image

analysis.time: Event period: January–August 2026; reporting week: 20–26 July 2026 (Week 30); publication date: 19 August 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Nigeria; five states (Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue, Edo) accounting for 86% of cases; 23 states and 116 local government areas reporting; predominantly young adults aged 21–30 years; healthcare workers at occupational risk.
analysis.event: Ongoing Lassa fever outbreak reported by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) as confirmed, with 1,000 cases and 237 deaths (case fatality rate 23.7%) as of epidemiological Week 30, 2026.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 1,000 confirmed cases; 237 deaths (CFR 23.7%); 17 new cases in Week 30; 1 new healthcare worker infection in Week 30; uneven geographical distribution concentrated in five states; young adults (21–30 years) most affected; rising CFR from 23.5% to 23.7%.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: NCDC Situation Report for Week 30 indicates continued surveillance, diagnostic services, and case management; new infections reported in Ondo, Bauchi, Edo, and Benue; sustained transmission in hotspot states; occupational risk to healthcare workers; public awareness and preventive measures emphasized; no evidence of travel restrictions or national emergency declared.

analysis.brief_en: Nigeria’s Lassa fever outbreak has reached 1,000 confirmed cases and 237 deaths as of late July 2026, with a case fatality rate of 23.7%. Five states—Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue, and Edo—account for 86% of cases, underscoring an uneven geographic burden. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention reports 17 new cases in the latest reporting week, including one infection among healthcare workers, highlighting ongoing occupational risks. Young adults aged 21–30 are the most affected group, reinforcing the need for targeted prevention in endemic communities. While new cases declined slightly from the prior week, the overall outbreak remains active, with health authorities maintaining surveillance and case management to limit further spread.
